investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T22:37–22:44Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to schedule remote agent pods. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" confirms zero remaining VM slots on those nodes, and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found. As a result, the eval probe's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never produced a running pod, so no evidence keys were written and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState was entirely unmet. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was unscheduled for 136s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=141947, confirming the probe ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, matching the contract gap.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 145s, no evidence keys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 142s, no evidence keys — all three checks share the same underlying scheduling failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a pod that never schedules means createAgent never returns a usable agent, so no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod does not start.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe-created agents. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and fully saturated.
Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), consuming VM slots and preventing new pods from scheduling.

Lower probability — a recent cluster resize or node drain reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger count, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding quota adjustment.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl shows available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after clearing no pods succeeds and produces all required evidence, the failure was transient rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured (e.g., targeting a label that no longer exists on any node), the primary cause would shift from resource exhaustion to a configuration drift in the pod spec.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have been recently reconfigured to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but the pod spec's affinity was not updated to include them, the root cause would be a pod spec/node label mismatch rather than pure capacity exhaustion.

If no existing pods are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (i.e., the resource shows as fully available but scheduling still fails), the extended resource plugin or node device plugin may be malfunctioning rather than the capacity being genuinely exhausted.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add an eval that verifies the count of currently running pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources stays below a defined threshold, alerting on potential slot leakage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a post-cleanup verification step to the remote-agent-create probe that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm-holding pods remain after withCleanup completes, catching cleanup regressions early.

Add a node-pool health eval that checks whether the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are in Ready state, catching node drain or capacity reduction events before they exhaust the scheduling pool.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T22:39–22:44Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the contract validation to fail with all four evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm node affinity have exhausted their allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota (peer-pod VM slots), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. The pod remains Unschedulable for ~136–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real inability to provision remote agent VMs, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are consumed by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for a new remote agent pod. Preemption confirms no evictable lower-priority pods exist on those nodes.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata-peerpods capable nodes), so the effective scheduling domain is already constrained to those 2 nodes, which are at capacity.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote agent demand: if multiple eval runs or real workloads are simultaneously holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the fixed pool of 2 eligible nodes may be structurally insufficient for the current load.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T22:37–22:44Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to schedule remote agent pods. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" confirms zero remaining VM slots on those nodes, and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found. As a result, the eval probe's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never produced a running pod, so no evidence keys were written and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState was entirely unmet. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was unscheduled for 136s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=141947, confirming the probe ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, matching the contract gap.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), pod stuck 145s, no evidence keys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 142s, no evidence keys — all three checks share the same underlying scheduling failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a pod that never schedules means createAgent never returns a usable agent, so no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod does not start.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe-created agents. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and fully saturated.
Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), consuming VM slots and preventing new pods from scheduling.

Lower probability — a recent cluster resize or node drain reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger count, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding quota adjustment.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl shows available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after clearing no pods succeeds and produces all required evidence, the failure was transient rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured (e.g., targeting a label that no longer exists on any node), the primary cause would shift from resource exhaustion to a configuration drift in the pod spec.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have been recently reconfigured to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but the pod spec's affinity was not updated to include them, the root cause would be a pod spec/node label mismatch rather than pure capacity exhaustion.

If no existing pods are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (i.e., the resource shows as fully available but scheduling still fails), the extended resource plugin or node device plugin may be malfunctioning rather than the capacity being genuinely exhausted.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add an eval that verifies the count of currently running pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources stays below a defined threshold, alerting on potential slot leakage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a post-cleanup verification step to the remote-agent-create probe that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm-holding pods remain after withCleanup completes, catching cleanup regressions early.

Add a node-pool health eval that checks whether the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are in Ready state, catching node drain or capacity reduction events before they exhaust the scheduling pool.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T22:39–22:44Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the contract validation to fail with all four evidence fields missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm node affinity have exhausted their allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota (peer-pod VM slots), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. The pod remains Unschedulable for ~136–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real inability to provision remote agent VMs, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata-peerpods capable nodes), so the effective scheduling domain is already constrained to those 2 nodes, which are at capacity.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote agent demand: if multiple eval runs or real workloads are simultaneously holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the fixed pool of 2 eligible nodes may be structurally insufficient for the current load.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 22:39 and 22:44 UTC on 2026-07-15 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence payload, causing all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be absent and the expected-output contract assertion on message to go unevaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector at all. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~136–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before timing out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-level failure observed by the AURA observability workflow.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM slots are a finite schedulable resource; concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up may have consumed all available slots, leaving none for the eval pod.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: only 2 nodes are eligible for remote agent pods by affinity/selector configuration; if those 2 nodes are at VM capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero regardless of total cluster size.

[Possible] Leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a prior eval run that did not complete cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have executed if a prior run was interrupted), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.
[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are undersized for concurrent eval demand, meaning the quota is structurally insufficient rather than temporarily exhausted.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster metrics show kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or configuration cause would need to be investigated.
If the pod scheduling error message changes on re-run (e.g., a different error unrelated to kata.peerpods.io/vm), the root cause would need to be revised.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and the pod schedules without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a persistent capacity problem.

If leaked pods from prior runs are not found in the production namespace, the stuck-cleanup hypothesis is disproved and the cause is more likely structural capacity insufficiency or a concurrent workload spike.

If the node affinity/selector configuration is confirmed unchanged and all 2 eligible nodes have available VM slots, the scheduling failure would not be reproducible and the incident may have been self-resolving.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., via the Kubernetes API or a cluster metrics endpoint) and warns when available slots fall below a safe threshold, so capacity exhaustion is detected before agent creation attempts fail.

Add a remote-agent-pod-cleanup eval or post-run assertion that verifies no orphaned remote agent pods remain in the production namespace after each eval cycle, catching withCleanup failures before they accumulate.

Add a remote-agent-scheduling-latency eval that measures pod scheduling time independently of agent readiness, so scheduling delays can be distinguished from agent startup or runtime failures in future diagnostics.
Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create with a short timeout specifically to detect scheduling failures early in the eval window, before the full runtime check is attempted.
